summary:
Ad Stars is an interactive 2.5D and retro-style 3D space mission simulator built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. Stepping into the role of an aerospace engineer inside a bustling Mission Control Center, players explore a pixel-art facility, customize suits, and take on 15 missions modeled after real space exploration programs—including lunar gateways, deep-space telescopes, planetary orbiters, and solar probes.

Before launch, players assemble spacecraft across four critical segments (Launch Vehicles, Spacecraft Buses, Scientific Instruments, and Ground Tracking Networks) while balancing budgets, payload mass, electrical power, and science output. They then validate local gravity, atmospheric density, drag coefficients, and thrust vectors in a pre-flight physics simulator against nominal mission corridors. Launches transition into a 320×240 retro 3D console featuring 15 mission-specific interactive minigames, such as ignition sequencing, hexagonal mirror alignment, and binary logic radiation shielding.

Built in TypeScript using custom HTML5 Canvas rendering, grid-based A* pathfinding, and zero-dependency procedural audio via the Web Audio API, Ad Stars offers real-time English and Portuguese localization and runs directly in desktop and mobile browsers.
details:
What It Does & How It WorksAd Stars is an interactive 2.5D and retro PS1-style 3D space mission simulator that places players in the role of an aerospace engineer inside a bustling Mission Control Center. The gameplay loop combines spatial exploration, hardware engineering, orbital physics, and real-time flight execution:

  • 2.5D Mission Control Hub: Players explore a pixel-art control facility, customize engineer suits, and interact with terminals while AI-driven scientists navigate the room using grid-based A* pathfinding with string-pulling smoothing.
  • Mission Board (15 Real-World Scenarios): Across 4 Career Maturity Levels (CML 1–4), players undertake missions modeled after real NASA programs, including Artemis Gateway, James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), Europa Clipper, Perseverance, Parker Solar Probe, DART, Dragonfly, and Voyager.
  • Engineering Workbench & Pre-Flight Physics Simulator: Before launch, players assemble spacecraft across four segments (Launchers, Spacecraft Buses, Scientific Instruments, and Ground Networks) while balancing budget, payload mass, electrical power, and science output. They then validate local gravity ($G$), atmospheric density, drag coefficient ($C_d$), and thrust vectors against nominal NASA mission corridors.
  • Retro 3D Launch Console & Flight Minigames: Launches transition into a 320×240 PS1-inspired 3D console featuring scanlines, dithering, and 15 mission-specific interactive protocols—such as ignition sequencing, cryogenic thermal calibration, hexagonal mirror alignment, binary logic radiation shielding, and Morse beacon decoding.

Benefits, Creativity & Intended Impact Aerospace engineering and orbital mechanics are often perceived as intimidating, abstract subjects. Ad Stars bridges that gap by blending nostalgic retro aesthetics with authentic NASA mission parameters and real-world propellant/payload trade-offs. Its creative approach turns complex engineering constraints—such as radiation shielding tiers, telemetry bandwidths, and center-of-mass torque—into tactile, high-stakes gameplay. Our intended impact is to inspire students and space enthusiasts worldwide to explore STEM fields and understand the real engineering behind NASA's current and future missions.

Tools, Languages & Design Considerations

  • Tech Stack: Built entirely in TypeScript using a custom HTML5 Canvas 2D/2.5D pixel-art engine and a software-rendered 320×240 3D console with affine texture projection and dynamic lighting.
  • Procedural Audio: All sound effects are synthesized in real time using the browser's native Web Audio API (AudioContext), eliminating external audio file dependencies.
  • Key Factors Considered: We prioritized 60 FPS performance optimization, cross-platform accessibility (supporting desktop keyboard/mouse and mobile touch D-pad controls), bilingual real-time localization (English and Portuguese), and instant browser access via Vercel deployment.

Source Code Repository

  • GitHub:https://github.com/luvasfarias-cloud/Ad-Stars---Nasa-Space-Apps-Challenge/tree/main

AI & Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure In accordance with the NASA Space Apps Challenge guidelines, we disclose that Large Language Models (LLMs) and AI coding assistants (Google AI Studio / Gemini) were used to accelerate development, structure TypeScript modules, optimize Canvas rendering loops, debug physics calculations, and format publicly available NASA mission parameters into bilingual (en/pt) data tables. All 2.5D/3D visuals are rendered programmatically via HTML5 Canvas, and all audio is synthesized via the Web Audio API. No NASA logos, flags, or official mission insignia were generated or modified using AI tools.
